catalog_locator: Ch. 2 Phonology, §2.4 'Stress', p. 17 (pdf p. 15 of the 2-up text-layer scan from archive.org item zamponi-maipure_2003; page image); §2.6.2 'Suprasegmental changes', p. 19 (pdf p. 16; image)
catalog_quote: Stress (generally marked in the original documents by a grave accent), exists in two degrees: primary stress and secondary stress. Primary stress falls on the antepenultimate, penultimate, or final syllable of the word. It is a suprasegmental phoneme of Maipure, as shown by the following minimal pairs: /kápi/ 'his hand' vs. /kapí/ 'you (sg.)' /núpa/ 'k.o. plant' vs. /nupá/ 'he is born' Secondary stress, not phonemic, seems to apply (avoiding sequences of two stressed syllables) to words of more than three syllables on one or, in the case of long words, more syllables to the left of the primary-stressed one. Consider, for example, the following forms from M1 and M4: tùmutúmu 'catarrh, cold', nutètakaná 'my companion (male)', nukumàɺakí 'my knee', wasùɺenámi 'his ghost', apèapèkipakí 'four', kaànikiwakanèkiní 'married woman'. The (final) position of the primary word stress can be derived in the sense that there are suffixes which always carry the main stress (see §2.6.2).
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Il prediletto sembra l' accento acuto sulle finali [...]. Reciterò alcune parole con quest' ordine, che le prime sieno Tamanache, e le seconde Maipùri. [...] Menitì campo, jomuchì granturco, tamanà nuvola, chipucù vento &c. Le particelle posposte a' nomi, sempre o quasi sempre son lunghe [...] Le voci dissillabe sono comunemente brevi sì nella lingua de' Tamanachi, che in quella de' Maipuri. [...] Le seguenti parole Tamanache, a cui soggiungeremo in fine le Maipùri, gli hanno sulla penultima: [...] urrùpu la stella, aràta la banana, araàri quì &c. [...] Non ricordami di altra variazione di accenti in queste due lingue.
new_statements.translation: The favourite seems to be the acute accent on final syllables [...]. I shall cite some words in this order, the first being Tamanaco and the second Maipure. [...] Menitì 'field', jomuchì 'maize', tamanà 'cloud', chipucù 'wind' etc. The particles postposed to nouns are always or almost always long (accented) [...] Disyllabic words are commonly short both in the language of the Tamanacos and in that of the Maipures. [...] The following Tamanaco words, to which we add the Maipure ones at the end, have it on the penultimate: [...] urrùpu 'star', aràta 'banana', araàri 'here' etc. [...] I do not recall any other variation of accents in these two languages.
new_statements.citation: Gilij, Filippo Salvadore. 1782. Saggio di storia americana.. Tomo III: Della religione, e delle lingue degli Orinochesi, e di altri Americani. Roma: Luigi Perego Erede Salvioni.
new_statements.locator: Tomo III, Appendice II, Capitolo VIII 'Dell'accento delle lingue Americane', pp. 311-312 (pdf pp. 333-334 of archive.org scan saggiodistoriaa04giligoog; page images / -)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: holds the Gilij 1782 Tomo III PDF (archive.org saggiodistoriaa04giligoog), two scanned texts, scandata, and 150-dpi page images of printed pp. 310-313 (pdf 332-335). I read the page images p. 311) and -p. 312) directly. The quoted passage is there exactly as transcribed (long-s normalised to s; the bracketed ellipses omit only the Tamanaco example words and the sentence 'in cambio del quale per costume introdotto, da noi Italiani viene adoperato il grave'). Full context, p. 311: 'Il prediletto sembra l' accento acuto sulle finali.. Reciterò alcune parole con quest' ordine, che le prime sieno Tamanache, e le seconde Maipùri. Accemà strada, chittimù.., toronò.., prutpetè testa &c.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Gilij (the only first-hand observer), Maipure word accent falls predominantly on the final syllable (including on postposed particles/suffixes, which attract it), but a set of words carries it on the penult instead, and disyllables commonly lack the final accent; no antepenultimate accent is reported for Maipure (only for Tamanaco). Placement is thus within the last two syllables and not stated as predictable — effectively lexical, final-dominant.
new_statements.exceptions: Penult-accented words (urrùpu, aràta, araàri); disyllables 'commonly short' (veni 'water', pitu 'your mother', iti 'name' written without final accent); postposed particles (almost) always accented.
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic 18th-century missionary description of citation forms, framed in terms of 'long/short' final vowels and acute/grave accent marks; word-level, with the remark that noun+postposed-particle groups take the accent on the particle. Gilij also marks accents throughout his Maipure grammar sketch (Libro III Cap. X, pp. 185-191) and texts, which Zamponi 2003 reanalyses.
new_statements.identity_note: Gilij's accent statement concerns Maipure proper (the language of his mission, 'i Maipuri'), contrasted throughout with Tamanaco (Cariban). Glottolog maip1247 'Maipure-Avane' lumps Maipure with Avane; Gilij treats Avane separately ('l'Avanè, dialetto del Maipure', Tomo III p. 156) and says nothing about Avane accent. All later work (Zamponi 2003, Ramirez 2001/2020) is reanalysis of Gilij's 1780s data; there is no other primary documentation.
